+## Importing over existing artwork
+
+Image **Replace** clears the entire destination layer, including pixels beneath transparent input. **Replace Frames** replaces the sheet as one operation and clears prior layer artwork in those frames. Unlock protected layers before either replacement; sheet replacement also refuses removal of locked frames. **New Layer**, **New Frame** and sheet append preserve existing pixels.

+# Import artwork safety — 9 October 2026
+
+This local repair follows the independent partial audit at `ad957550f6656b82f5f35162c8eabc19a45a1473`. The original audit and its failed reproductions remain unchanged under the local `audit/` directory. This record does not certify every feature, a deployed release or the full compiled suite.
+
+## Repair scope
+
+| Finding | Change and acceptance boundary |
+| --- | --- |
+| C01 | Imports publish fresh raster ownership, immutable frames, dirty/edit revision and buffer revision in one workspace transaction. Native canaries check immediate pixels and autosaved reload without a manual Save or repaint helper. |
+| H02 | Import constructs its prospective destinations directly rather than falling back to the active layer after a refused add action. Metadata, capacity, palette, memory and history failures preserve the prior workspace. |
+| H03 | One structural snapshot covers original pixels, frame/layer metadata, optional palettes and original dimensions. Redo admission uses destination dimensions. Previously lazy affected layers receive explicit transparent original snapshots. |
+| H04 | Six links to ignored files are now explicitly labeled local-only references. The documentation checker rejects existing local targets absent from the publishable file set, including ignored files; directories must contain publishable descendants. Local audit copies are outside current documentation/compiler inputs. |
+| M05 | Each replaced layer receives a new transparent surface, so transparent input cannot retain old pixels. Native tests cover full-size and smaller inputs. |
+| M06 | Replace refuses a locked active layer; sheet replacement refuses any locked existing layer, including frames it would delete. |
+| M07 | Failed hydration restores the immutable original session, native-file association, raster registry and history transaction. Dirty state, selection/mask, revisions and Undo/Redo survive publication failure and even a second observer exception. |
+| M08 | Mitigation: the byte-copy canvas fixture explicitly documents its limits. Native canaries cover transparency, refusal, locks, grouped history and persistence; arbitrary blending, transforms and scaling are not established by this mock. |
+| L10 | Coverage includes application TypeScript/TSX sources outside `src/types/**`. Both gates and their CI callers enforce the existing coverage thresholds; default unit concurrency is two workers. The excluded directory also contains two runtime project-format constants. |
+
+Native follow-up exposed two additional integration gaps. Undo on a previously lazy layer originally retained the imported buffer; explicit blank snapshots repair it. A synchronous post-resize render originally used stale callback dimensions and could crop the restored raster. The viewport now reads committed dimensions for imperative composites and layer lookup. A native resize/Undo/Redo/reload canary retains an original corner pixel.
+
+## Original repair verification
+
+| Final check | Executed result and scope |
+| --- | --- |
+| Full gate | All five stages passed in 142.89 seconds: clean-checkout documentation targets, strict types, warning-free lint, coverage/unit assertions and production build. The standard gate's four shared stages passed within this full invocation. |
+| Units | **2,120 passes /201 suites**, two workers, with coverage. |
+| Configured-source unit coverage | **69.18% statements, 62.41% branches, 61.49% functions, 70.47% lines**; original thresholds unchanged. Unexecuted workers/UI remain visible in the denominator; `src/types/**` is excluded. |

+| External TestSprite | **Blocked service verdict; audited inconclusive** for the complete saved-artwork plan. Run-pinned steps show repeated canvas clicks without establishing the required stroke; failure-bundle retrieval was withheld by the service. |

The three final browser fixtures wait for document parsing and explicit restored-canvas readiness rather than the global load event. Strict types and scoped lint were rerun for this test-only refinement. The application sources and compiled build remained unchanged. +
+TestSprite CLI 0.13.0 ran existing test `b99a9888-2ca0-4353-a3f7-05dbfec14f6d`, “Challenge: Reloaded artwork survives new edits, Undo, Redo and a second saved reload”, against the frozen compiled build on local port 3101. The trace contains no completed Undo/Redo actions. The run-pinned steps were retrieved successfully, but the full bundle/video was not inspected. The [TestSprite execution](https://www.testsprite.com/dashboard-v3/o/8da317b3-5f3e-506d-b110-a2ae9c2af7b8/projects/ad7cf58e-3c0f-41d6-96a8-a3a076faf639/execution/ce4a3e17-10d2-4634-8641-00bea49cb830) retains the service record. The configured development Turbopack startup issue is separate from production compilation. +The service worker captures its original cache handle at event arrival. Optional opening, reads and writes settle after rejection, synchronous exception or a 250 ms deadline. Static resources start their healthy network fetch immediately; default resources keep cache-first behavior and try the network after unavailable storage. Default opening and reading have separate deadlines and can together take up to 500 ms. Deadlines settle responses/event lifetimes; they do not abort native storage operations. A cache response arriving after its deadline is unavailable to that fallback; physical-device cache latency remains unqualified.
+
+Readable cached resources remain usable offline. A failed HTTP refresh also prefers a readable cached response. Unavailable cache plus failed network returns an explicit resource error, never substituted HTML. Worker bootstrap fragments retain the existing synthetic-response handling. Mandatory installation still requires a complete offline shell; activation and waiting-update ownership contracts remain intact. Warming uses the originally captured handle and does not reopen a retired bucket.
+
+## Retained failures and repairs
+
+- Before repair, emitted-worker probes: 15 failures /3 passes across 18 cases. The first harness attempt also recorded unhandled rejection noise; the corrected baseline retains the same 15 failures without that harness noise.
+- Before repair, native Chromium `open-reject`: Studio HTML loaded but active restoration did not finish after reload. Its trace and screenshot remain retained.
+- A preliminary candidate passed its full gate, but an additional HTTP-503 refresh check exposed a new race: the failed network response beat a readable cached 200. That failing check is retained. The repaired policy now prefers the readable cache; 54 focused checks across four files pass.
+- Final emitted-worker resource suite: 26 cases cover rejected/stalled opening, reads and writes; synchronous storage errors; exact cached bytes; failed refresh; bounded event lifetimes; unavailable offline resources and warming.
+- Prior documentation-only CI replay [37986316428](https://github.com/lxcario/PixiBun/actions/runs/37986316428), `5cdf03d`: 2,199 passes /one failure. Nearest-neighbor identity correctness exceeded its 5,000 ms runner timeout, reporting 6,288 ms. Performance/build/browser jobs did not complete. This does not rewrite the earlier `94bd345` passing run.
+- Byte comparison now uses native buffer equality for every byte of both the transformed output and unchanged input at all four original resolutions. Test count, default timeout, coverage policy and separate warmed performance limits are unchanged.
+- First scoped native candidate run: 29 passes /one failure, no retries. All 12 new fault cases pass across Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, restoring exact saved artwork and resource hashes. The existing Firefox drawing case completed all final application assertions, then failed `Browser.removeBrowserContext` with `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` during context teardown. Trace assessment is retained; the cause is not established, and this run remains failed.
+
+## Executed candidate checks
+
+The fresh six-stage local gate passes 2,226 tests /203 suites, documentation, strict types, lint, coverage, separate performance limits and production build. Coverage is 69.17% statements, 62.39% branches, 61.49% functions, 70.46% lines. RotSprite p90 of warmed batch means is 5.801 ms against the unchanged 10 ms limit. A preceding final-app gate measured 3.093 ms and also passed. These desktop batch measurements do not qualify individual-call latency or physical-device frame rates.
+
+Qualified local build: `IHzbF9f6G4oaf-1wpkS95`, 259 compiled files. Selected source/validation inputs: 706, aggregate `424774cc47769c984417021cb351a0d037abe31be57cfcb3046ca5e6fadb5d12`. Build/source freeze receipts bind subsequent runs to this candidate. The normal five-stage pre-push gate independently passes all 2,226 tests and publishes the two repair commits to the existing draft review branch.
+
+CI run [37992174340](https://github.com/lxcario/PixiBun/actions/runs/37992174340) passes its six-stage gate on Node 22.14.0, all 2,226 tests /203 suites and the unchanged performance limits. RotSprite warmed batch p90 is 2.253 ms. Its merge `cb00150c07fc58e2eb01bb09d21949ddc79dd162` and local candidate have the same Git tree, `9622eb475ec1d020cc06b717800204e32a5c1b54`. Automatic CI retrieval compares all 379 indexed files and original index bytes. The independently retrieved ZIP also matches its API digest; all embedded indexed files and the file set match locally.
+
+Fresh two-build replay: five passes /one measured Windows WebKit legacy-Blob fixture refusal, one worker and zero retries. All 259 previous compiled files match before and after. Native attachment records identify the actual buckets as `pixibun-v1.14.1-ad957550f6656b82f5f35162c8eabc19a45a1473` and `pixibun-v1.14.1-bd4a352090836792a647bfd3ad5025f77b2c183b` and preserve the artwork and optional metadata through update and rollback. This local proxy transition does not qualify production-host deployment or actual Safari legacy rollback.

The API-verified reports are retained before their seven-day artifact expiry. Passing configured score thresholds does not close the remaining target/manual findings.

The refined fixture requires a nondecreasing timestamp and still compares every other document field and every native PNG byte. Its second run passed five cases and failed legacy-Blob preparation in Windows WebKit. The diagnostic captured `UnknownError: Error preparing Blob/File data to be stored in object store`, matching the [previously recorded Windows WebKit storage limitation](phase-implementation-status.md). The final guard skips only that measured error on Windows WebKit, after verifying atomic refusal leaves the prior document, stored bytes and visible artwork intact. +
+## Development, external verification and remote custody
+
+The configured Node 22 Turbopack process started successfully with its existing development cache; its first measured Studio response was HTTP 200 in 1.06 seconds. The complete development suite passes **196/196**, zero skips/failures, one worker and zero retries, in 12.5 minutes. A second fresh process with the old `.next/dev` preserved aside reported ready in 458 ms; its first observed Studio request compiled and returned in 4.4 seconds. The later explicit HTTP probe took 180 ms after that request had already warmed the route. A fresh-browser drawing/save/native-reload smoke passed on this process too. This separates cache-assisted suite execution from empty-cache startup rather than labeling both cold. The earlier startup probe that exceeded 30 seconds remains preserved. No Webpack fallback was used in these runs.
+
+Future GitHub CI logs, coverage and browser evidence use revision/run/attempt artifact names, file hash indexes and explicit 90-day retention, including failed runs. The browser workflow uses one worker and zero retries and runs production checks even if development checks fail, once its production build succeeds. [GitHub's retention policy](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/configuring-the-retention-period-for-github-actions-artifacts-and-logs-in-your-organization) caps public-repository artifact retention at 90 days. +

That failed remote run is preserved independently of local repair checks. Candidate remote CI and the new TestSprite layout run remain pending here; the original blocked/inconclusive TestSprite artwork run is unchanged.
+

+
+Raw logs, structured results, frozen manifests and retained native failure bundles are under local-only `artifacts/l09-repeatability-2026-10-09/`. Failed runs are separate from successful reruns. The [local verification receipt](evidence/2026-10-09-validation-repeatability/verification.json) records 38 evidence hashes and the exact local scope without embedding signed recording links or credentials. +

Automated browser/Axe/keyboard checks qualify their executed states and retain the documented compact color-dock target-size tradeoff. No physical-device or WCAG-conformance result is inferred from them.

Application source is unchanged from the resource-recovery repair. Both previous failed runs and new verdicts retain their own revisions.
+
+## Recovery behavior
+
+The service worker captures its original cache handle at event arrival. Optional opening, reads and writes settle after rejection, synchronous exception or a 250 ms deadline. Static resources start their healthy network fetch immediately; default resources keep cache-first behavior and try the network after unavailable storage. Default opening and reading have separate deadlines and can together take up to 500 ms. Deadlines settle responses/event lifetimes; they do not abort native storage operations. A cache response arriving after its deadline is unavailable to that fallback; physical-device cache latency remains unqualified.
+
+Readable cached resources remain usable offline. A failed HTTP refresh also prefers a readable cached response. Unavailable cache plus failed network returns an explicit resource error, never substituted HTML. Worker bootstrap fragments retain the existing synthetic-response handling. Mandatory installation still requires a complete offline shell; activation and waiting-update ownership contracts remain intact. Warming uses the originally captured handle and does not reopen a retired bucket.
+
+## Retained failures and repairs
+
+- Before repair, emitted-worker probes: 15 failures /3 passes across 18 cases. The first harness attempt also recorded unhandled rejection noise; the corrected baseline retains the same 15 failures without that harness noise.
+- Before repair, native Chromium `open-reject`: Studio HTML loaded but active restoration did not finish after reload. Its trace and screenshot remain retained.

+- First scoped native candidate run: 29 passes /one failure, no retries. All 12 new fault cases pass across Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, restoring exact saved artwork and resource hashes. The existing Firefox drawing case completed all final application assertions, then failed `Browser.removeBrowserContext` with `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` during context teardown. Trace assessment is retained; the cause is not established, and this run remains failed.
+

+
+The fresh six-stage local gate passes 2,226 tests /203 suites, documentation, strict types, lint, coverage, separate performance limits and production build. Coverage is 69.17% statements, 62.39% branches, 61.49% functions, 70.46% lines. RotSprite p90 of warmed batch means is 5.801 ms against the unchanged 10 ms limit. A preceding final-app gate measured 3.093 ms and also passed. These desktop batch measurements do not qualify individual-call latency or physical-device frame rates.

+## Importing over existing artwork
+
+Image **Replace** clears the entire destination layer, including pixels beneath transparent input. **Replace Frames** replaces the sheet as one operation and clears prior layer artwork in those frames. Unlock protected layers before either replacement; sheet replacement also refuses removal of locked frames. **New Layer**, **New Frame** and sheet append preserve existing pixels.
+
+An admitted image import records one Undo step for its pixels, layer/frame changes, canvas resize and optional palette. If capacity, metadata, Undo memory or staging fails, the import stays open and the existing drawing is preserved. Successful imports repaint and schedule autosave; wait for Saved before closing. Undo is a session aid, not a portable backup.
+
 ## Practicing without replacing your drawing
 
 Desktop Playground saves a checkpoint of your original before opening separate practice. **Return to drawing** restores it; **Keep practice in Studio** saves a new project first. Practice has no autosave. A refresh loses unkept practice, while Return restores the saved original through normal admission. Session Undo/Redo and native-file handles are not portable. If the checkpoint or Keep fails, stay on the page and read the warning; your original is not replaced by practice. [Step-by-step practice and return](learning-and-playground.md#keep-your-drawing-try-something-new).

+# L09 validation repeatability — 9 October 2026
+
+The local milestone is supported by two passing full gates and a complete production-browser verdict: **338 passed /7 capability skips /zero failures**, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, one worker and zero retries. The [earlier import repair and independent replay](2026-10-09-import-artwork-safety.md) retain their original passing and failing outcomes. This record does not certify every source file or approve a release.
+
+## Timing policy and baseline
+
+RotSprite speed now runs in `scripts/benchmarkRotSprite.mjs`, outside Vitest and V8 coverage. Its original 23×12 hollow outline and 50 angles remain unchanged. Each independent Node 22 process warms all angles for five batches, then records 15 serial batches. The metric is milliseconds per rotation averaged within each 50-call batch; the limit remains **p90 <10 ms**. Baselines never recalibrate that limit. The algorithm is unchanged. Contour, ring-connectivity and fractional-pivot correctness remains in coverage, with existing coverage requirements unchanged.
+
+| Invocation | Median ms | P90 ms | Limit ms |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Baseline 1 | 2.932902 | 3.166656 | 10 |
+| Baseline 2 | 2.560634 | 3.124944 | 10 |
+| Baseline 3 | 2.303532 | 3.227008 | 10 |
+| Full gate 2 | 2.964974 | 3.319112 | 10 |
+| Full gate 3 | 2.857062 | 3.171918 | 10 |
+
+These are controlled Windows x64 host measurements on an Intel Core i5-12500H (16 logical CPUs), Node 22.23.3 and TypeScript 5.9.3, not device latency or arbitrary sprite-size guarantees. Other coarse unit timeouts remain execution bounds; this change separates the failing RotSprite speed assertion specifically. The independent instrumented failures at 11.55 ms and 10.63 ms remain failed evidence.
+
+## Gates and frozen production build
+
+Both six-stage gates pass documentation, strict types, lint, **2,122 correctness tests /201 suites with coverage**, the separate benchmark and production compilation. Gate 2 took 296.50 seconds; gate 3 took 235.75 seconds. Gate 3 coverage is 69.18% statements, 62.39% branches, 61.49% functions and 70.46% lines. Coverage still excludes `src/types/**`, including its runtime format constants.
+
+The first gate failed with 2,120 passing tests and two failing existing service-worker fixtures that still passed a cache name to the changed helper. Updating those fixtures to pass their owned Cache object restored their LRU/shell checks; 24 focused tests passed before the two full gates. The failed invocation remains preserved.
+
+Production build **`vRByH4JDPWpOHZ6RE4Czj`**, cache `pixibun-l09-candidate-20261009`, ran all **345 cases /31 files** in 40.8 minutes. Its 694 runtime/validation inputs hash to `84b387ab1f6da21016d77aea952a4ff4a7ae7f86008d3611d6d52610535a53cd`; its 259 compiled server/static/BUILD_ID files hash to `f16646639214a1b16cd1938aa429d98876dc51eaffab06353579a6509b8be36f`. Every frozen file matched after the run. No production expectation or application source changed during it. The seven skips are browser capability cases, not passes. All 21 import-safety cases and six worker-transition cases pass in this complete run.
+
+## Retained Firefox failure and worker ownership
+
+The original full-run trace shows the old and new cache names persisting throughout the ten-second cleanup assertion. It does not record enough ordering to prove which write recreated the old bucket. The source nevertheless allowed a delayed response to reopen its old cache by name after the new worker deleted it. Three emitted-worker VM cases reproduced this mechanism for navigation, static and default requests before the fix.
+
+Responses now retain their original Cache object for writes and trimming; queued warming captures ownership before waiting. A deleted Cache handle can receive a late write without recreating its named bucket. Static background work also registers its lifetime while the response remains pending. The three deterministic regressions and the existing route/lifecycle tests pass. The complete native suite passes both ordinary waiting activation and deliberately delayed old writes in all three engines. This supports the repaired mechanism and this broad run; it does not establish universal lifecycle stability from one trace.
+
+## Actual application update and rollback
+
+The separate release fixture uses the preserved compatible build **`kbrD0Z2xKkmvlgI2y3Dd7`** and the frozen candidate on one local origin. The older 259 compiled files still match their original manifest `5ce717ef19a90897b4c14459f6d48100de11f803b95689454fce92afc0b41a30`.
+
+Final result: **five passes /one measured capability skip**, one worker, zero retries. Chromium and Firefox pass both native ArrayBuffer and legacy Blob fixtures. WebKit passes the current ArrayBuffer path. The journey checks a refused shell installation, saved and dirty tabs, waiting instructions without forced refresh, activation after all tabs close, artwork identity, editable rig/ramp metadata, native pixel bytes, candidate save-back, rollback editing and an offline reopen. The local host retains both builds' static assets; production hosting skew protection remains separate.
+
+The first run recorded two passes and four failures. Three final assertions expected `updatedAt` to remain byte-identical even though the existing visibility/pagehide handler saves again on close. The refined fixture requires a nondecreasing timestamp and still compares every other document field and every native PNG byte. Its second run passed five cases and failed legacy-Blob preparation in Windows WebKit. The diagnostic captured `UnknownError: Error preparing Blob/File data to be stored in object store`, matching the [previously recorded Windows WebKit storage limitation](phase-implementation-status.md). The final guard skips only that measured error on Windows WebKit, after verifying atomic refusal leaves the prior document, stored bytes and visible artwork intact. Legacy-Blob rollback on Safari remains unqualified. The initial failures, second-run failure and diagnostic trace remain preserved.
+
+Only the new release fixture was refined after the production run. Strict types and scoped lint passed after the refinements; the application and complete production-suite inputs remain unchanged. The final 694-input fingerprint is `daa72a965265f7b418f04ed9e4c77494c3235ca624ae46118e57bbe25445a49a`; the original frozen manifest remains preserved separately.
+
+## Development, external verification and remote custody
+
+The configured Node 22 Turbopack process started successfully with its existing development cache; its first measured Studio response was HTTP 200 in 1.06 seconds. The complete development suite passes **196/196**, zero skips/failures, one worker and zero retries, in 12.5 minutes. A second fresh process with the old `.next/dev` preserved aside reported ready in 458 ms; its first observed Studio request compiled and returned in 4.4 seconds. The later explicit HTTP probe took 180 ms after that request had already warmed the route. A fresh-browser drawing/save/native-reload smoke passed on this process too. This separates cache-assisted suite execution from empty-cache startup rather than labeling both cold. The earlier startup probe that exceeded 30 seconds remains preserved. Application CSS discovery is now explicitly scoped to `src`, and ignored local audit/copy/evidence files cannot supply CSS classes; [Tailwind's source-base guidance](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files) documents the syntax. No Webpack fallback was used in these runs.
+
+Future GitHub CI logs, coverage and browser evidence use revision/run/attempt artifact names, file hash indexes and explicit 90-day retention, including failed runs. The browser workflow uses one worker and zero retries and runs production checks even if development checks fail, once its production build succeeds. [GitHub's retention policy](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/configuring-the-retention-period-for-github-actions-artifacts-and-logs-in-your-organization) caps public-repository artifact retention at 90 days. Selected candidate results and failed traces will also be preserved in a separate draft verification archive in the existing repository, with upload/retrieval hashes; it stores evidence rather than approving an application release. Index generation is tested locally; candidate CI upload, archive upload, retrieval and digest verification are pending at this source checkpoint. Historical tracked evidence has not been removed.
+
+The existing base-revision remote CI failed documentation at the six ignored-file links, leaving browser and Lighthouse jobs skipped. That failed remote run is preserved independently of local repair checks. Candidate remote CI and the new TestSprite layout run remain pending here; the original blocked/inconclusive TestSprite artwork run is unchanged.
+
+## Evidence and remaining release limits
+
+Raw logs, structured results, frozen manifests and retained native failure bundles are under local-only `artifacts/l09-repeatability-2026-10-09/`. Failed runs are separate from successful reruns. The [local verification receipt](evidence/2026-10-09-validation-repeatability/verification.json) records 38 evidence hashes and the exact local scope without embedding signed recording links or credentials. Remote CI, external and archive-custody receipts are subsequent evidence, not implied by this local checkpoint. The final documentation-only check first failed on a sandbox temporary-cache rename restriction; its native workspace-cache retry is recorded separately.
+
+Physical pen/touch devices, manual screen-reader observations, low-memory/long-session and real two-machine/network modes, actual production-host update/rollback and final release approval remain separate. Automated browser/Axe/keyboard checks qualify their executed states and retain the documented compact color-dock target-size tradeoff. No physical-device or WCAG-conformance result is inferred from them.

+# S1 resource-cache recovery and L09 replay — 10 October 2026
+
+Application repair: `8e43eb7469beb22b92d59ff8a954f573ddece9d3`. Validation-only byte-comparison repair: `bd4a352090836792a647bfd3ad5025f77b2c183b`. The latter changes no application source. Work started on 9 October and continued after midnight in Europe/Istanbul. Evidence paths retain their initial session date.
+
+Latest validation-only follow-up: `2591829e403d543a15efe169aba4127edd137385`. It observes native activation before reopening a window and uses full Chromium headless mode for development. Application source is unchanged from the resource-recovery repair. Both previous failed runs and new verdicts retain their own revisions.
+
+## Recovery behavior
+
+The service worker captures its original cache handle at event arrival. Optional opening, reads and writes settle after rejection, synchronous exception or a 250 ms deadline. Static resources start their healthy network fetch immediately; default resources keep cache-first behavior and try the network after unavailable storage. Default opening and reading have separate deadlines and can together take up to 500 ms. Deadlines settle responses/event lifetimes; they do not abort native storage operations. A cache response arriving after its deadline is unavailable to that fallback; physical-device cache latency remains unqualified.
+
+Readable cached resources remain usable offline. A failed HTTP refresh also prefers a readable cached response. Unavailable cache plus failed network returns an explicit resource error, never substituted HTML. Worker bootstrap fragments retain the existing synthetic-response handling. Mandatory installation still requires a complete offline shell; activation and waiting-update ownership contracts remain intact. Warming uses the originally captured handle and does not reopen a retired bucket.
+
+## Retained failures and repairs
+
+- Before repair, emitted-worker probes: 15 failures /3 passes across 18 cases. The first harness attempt also recorded unhandled rejection noise; the corrected baseline retains the same 15 failures without that harness noise.
+- Before repair, native Chromium `open-reject`: Studio HTML loaded but active restoration did not finish after reload. Its trace and screenshot remain retained.
+- A preliminary candidate passed its full gate, but an additional HTTP-503 refresh check exposed a new race: the failed network response beat a readable cached 200. That failing check is retained. The repaired policy now prefers the readable cache; 54 focused checks across four files pass.
+- Final emitted-worker resource suite: 26 cases cover rejected/stalled opening, reads and writes; synchronous storage errors; exact cached bytes; failed refresh; bounded event lifetimes; unavailable offline resources and warming.
+- Prior documentation-only CI replay [37986316428](https://github.com/lxcario/PixiBun/actions/runs/37986316428), `5cdf03d`: 2,199 passes /one failure. Nearest-neighbor identity correctness exceeded its 5,000 ms runner timeout, reporting 6,288 ms. Performance/build/browser jobs did not complete. This does not rewrite the earlier `94bd345` passing run.
+- Byte comparison now uses native buffer equality for every byte of both the transformed output and unchanged input at all four original resolutions. Test count, default timeout, coverage policy and separate warmed performance limits are unchanged.
+- First scoped native candidate run: 29 passes /one failure, no retries. All 12 new fault cases pass across Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, restoring exact saved artwork and resource hashes. The existing Firefox drawing case completed all final application assertions, then failed `Browser.removeBrowserContext` with `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` during context teardown. Trace assessment is retained; the cause is not established, and this run remains failed.
+
+## Executed candidate checks
+
+The fresh six-stage local gate passes 2,226 tests /203 suites, documentation, strict types, lint, coverage, separate performance limits and production build. Coverage is 69.17% statements, 62.39% branches, 61.49% functions, 70.46% lines. RotSprite p90 of warmed batch means is 5.801 ms against the unchanged 10 ms limit. A preceding final-app gate measured 3.093 ms and also passed. These desktop batch measurements do not qualify individual-call latency or physical-device frame rates.
+
+Qualified local build: `IHzbF9f6G4oaf-1wpkS95`, 259 compiled files. Selected source/validation inputs: 706, aggregate `424774cc47769c984417021cb351a0d037abe31be57cfcb3046ca5e6fadb5d12`. Build/source freeze receipts bind subsequent runs to this candidate. The normal five-stage pre-push gate independently passes all 2,226 tests and publishes the two repair commits to the existing draft review branch.
+
+CI run [37992174340](https://github.com/lxcario/PixiBun/actions/runs/37992174340) passes its six-stage gate on Node 22.14.0, all 2,226 tests /203 suites and the unchanged performance limits. RotSprite warmed batch p90 is 2.253 ms. Its merge `cb00150c07fc58e2eb01bb09d21949ddc79dd162` and local candidate have the same Git tree, `9622eb475ec1d020cc06b717800204e32a5c1b54`. Automatic CI retrieval compares all 379 indexed files and original index bytes. The independently retrieved ZIP also matches its API digest; all embedded indexed files and the file set match locally.
+
+Fresh two-build replay: five passes /one measured Windows WebKit legacy-Blob fixture refusal, one worker and zero retries. All 259 previous compiled files match before and after. Native attachment records identify the actual buckets as `pixibun-v1.14.1-ad957550f6656b82f5f35162c8eabc19a45a1473` and `pixibun-v1.14.1-bd4a352090836792a647bfd3ad5025f77b2c183b` and preserve the artwork and optional metadata through update and rollback. This local proxy transition does not qualify production-host deployment or actual Safari legacy rollback.
+

The API-verified reports are retained before their seven-day artifact expiry. Passing configured score thresholds does not close the remaining target/manual findings.

+

+## Repair scope
+
+| Finding | Change and acceptance boundary |
+| --- | --- |
+| C01 | Imports publish fresh raster ownership, immutable frames, dirty/edit revision and buffer revision in one workspace transaction. Native canaries check immediate pixels and autosaved reload without a manual Save or repaint helper. |
+| H02 | Import constructs its prospective destinations directly rather than falling back to the active layer after a refused add action. Metadata, capacity, palette, memory and history failures preserve the prior workspace. |
+| H03 | One structural snapshot covers original pixels, frame/layer metadata, optional palettes and original dimensions. Redo admission uses destination dimensions. Previously lazy affected layers receive explicit transparent original snapshots. |
+| H04 | Six links to ignored files are now explicitly labeled local-only references. The documentation checker rejects existing local targets absent from the publishable file set, including ignored files; directories must contain publishable descendants. Local audit copies are outside current documentation/compiler inputs. |
+| M05 | Each replaced layer receives a new transparent surface, so transparent input cannot retain old pixels. Native tests cover full-size and smaller inputs. |
+| M06 | Replace refuses a locked active layer; sheet replacement refuses any locked existing layer, including frames it would delete. |
+| M07 | Failed hydration restores the immutable original session, native-file association, raster registry and history transaction. Dirty state, selection/mask, revisions and Undo/Redo survive publication failure and even a second observer exception. |

A native resize/Undo/Redo/reload canary retains an original corner pixel.

+# L09 validation repeatability — 9 October 2026
+
+The local milestone is supported by two passing full gates and a complete production-browser verdict: **338 passed /7 capability skips /zero failures**, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, one worker and zero retries. The [earlier import repair and independent replay](2026-10-09-import-artwork-safety.md) retain their original passing and failing outcomes. This record does not certify every source file or approve a release.
+
+## Timing policy and baseline
+
+RotSprite speed now runs in `scripts/benchmarkRotSprite.mjs`, outside Vitest and V8 coverage. Its original 23×12 hollow outline and 50 angles remain unchanged. Each independent Node 22 process warms all angles for five batches, then records 15 serial batches. The metric is milliseconds per rotation averaged within each 50-call batch; the limit remains **p90 <10 ms**. Baselines never recalibrate that limit. The algorithm is unchanged. Contour, ring-connectivity and fractional-pivot correctness remains in coverage, with existing coverage requirements unchanged.
+
+| Invocation | Median ms | P90 ms | Limit ms |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Baseline 1 | 2.932902 | 3.166656 | 10 |
+| Baseline 2 | 2.560634 | 3.124944 | 10 |
+| Baseline 3 | 2.303532 | 3.227008 | 10 |
+| Full gate 2 | 2.964974 | 3.319112 | 10 |
+| Full gate 3 | 2.857062 | 3.171918 | 10 |
+
+These are controlled Windows x64 host measurements on an Intel Core i5-12500H (16 logical CPUs), Node 22.23.3 and TypeScript 5.9.3, not device latency or arbitrary sprite-size guarantees. Other coarse unit timeouts remain execution bounds; this change separates the failing RotSprite speed assertion specifically. The independent instrumented failures at 11.55 ms and 10.63 ms remain failed evidence.
+
+## Gates and frozen production build
+
+Both six-stage gates pass documentation, strict types, lint, **2,122 correctness tests /201 suites with coverage**, the separate benchmark and production compilation. Gate 2 took 296.50 seconds; gate 3 took 235.75 seconds. Gate 3 coverage is 69.18% statements, 62.39% branches, 61.49% functions and 70.46% lines. Coverage still excludes `src/types/**`, including its runtime format constants.
+
+The first gate failed with 2,120 passing tests and two failing existing service-worker fixtures that still passed a cache name to the changed helper. Updating those fixtures to pass their owned Cache object restored their LRU/shell checks; 24 focused tests passed before the two full gates. The failed invocation remains preserved.
+
+Production build **`vRByH4JDPWpOHZ6RE4Czj`**, cache `pixibun-l09-candidate-20261009`, ran all **345 cases /31 files** in 40.8 minutes. Its 694 runtime/validation inputs hash to `84b387ab1f6da21016d77aea952a4ff4a7ae7f86008d3611d6d52610535a53cd`; its 259 compiled server/static/BUILD_ID files hash to `f16646639214a1b16cd1938aa429d98876dc51eaffab06353579a6509b8be36f`. Every frozen file matched after the run. No production expectation or application source changed during it. The seven skips are browser capability cases, not passes. All 21 import-safety cases and six worker-transition cases pass in this complete run.
+
+## Retained Firefox failure and worker ownership
+
+The original full-run trace shows the old and new cache names persisting throughout the ten-second cleanup assertion. It does not record enough ordering to prove which write recreated the old bucket. The source nevertheless allowed a delayed response to reopen its old cache by name after the new worker deleted it. Three emitted-worker VM cases reproduced this mechanism for navigation, static and default requests before the fix.
+
+Responses now retain their original Cache object for writes and trimming; queued warming captures ownership before waiting. A deleted Cache handle can receive a late write without recreating its named bucket. Static background work also registers its lifetime while the response remains pending. The three deterministic regressions and the existing route/lifecycle tests pass. The complete native suite passes both ordinary waiting activation and deliberately delayed old writes in all three engines. This supports the repaired mechanism and this broad run; it does not establish universal lifecycle stability from one trace.
+
+## Actual application update and rollback
+
+The separate release fixture uses the preserved compatible build **`kbrD0Z2xKkmvlgI2y3Dd7`** and the frozen candidate on one local origin. The older 259 compiled files still match their original manifest `5ce717ef19a90897b4c14459f6d48100de11f803b95689454fce92afc0b41a30`.
+
+Final result: **five passes /one measured capability skip**, one worker, zero retries. Chromium and Firefox pass both native ArrayBuffer and legacy Blob fixtures. WebKit passes the current ArrayBuffer path. The journey checks a refused shell installation, saved and dirty tabs, waiting instructions without forced refresh, activation after all tabs close, artwork identity, editable rig/ramp metadata, native pixel bytes, candidate save-back, rollback editing and an offline reopen. The local host retains both builds' static assets; production hosting skew protection remains separate.
+
+The first run recorded two passes and four failures. Three final assertions expected `updatedAt` to remain byte-identical even though the existing visibility/pagehide handler saves again on close. The refined fixture requires a nondecreasing timestamp and still compares every other document field and every native PNG byte. Its second run passed five cases and failed legacy-Blob preparation in Windows WebKit. The diagnostic captured `UnknownError: Error preparing Blob/File data to be stored in object store`, matching the [previously recorded Windows WebKit storage limitation](phase-implementation-status.md). The final guard skips only that measured error on Windows WebKit, after verifying atomic refusal leaves the prior document, stored bytes and visible artwork intact. Legacy-Blob rollback on Safari remains unqualified. The initial failures, second-run failure and diagnostic trace remain preserved.
+
+Only the new release fixture was refined after the production run. Strict types and scoped lint passed after the refinements; the application and complete production-suite inputs remain unchanged. The final 694-input fingerprint is `daa72a965265f7b418f04ed9e4c77494c3235ca624ae46118e57bbe25445a49a`; the original frozen manifest remains preserved separately.
+
+## Development, external verification and remote custody
+
+The configured Node 22 Turbopack process started successfully with its existing development cache; its first measured Studio response was HTTP 200 in 1.06 seconds. The complete development suite passes **196/196**, zero skips/failures, one worker and zero retries, in 12.5 minutes. A second fresh process with the old `.next/dev` preserved aside reported ready in 458 ms; its first observed Studio request compiled and returned in 4.4 seconds. The later explicit HTTP probe took 180 ms after that request had already warmed the route. A fresh-browser drawing/save/native-reload smoke passed on this process too. This separates cache-assisted suite execution from empty-cache startup rather than labeling both cold. The earlier startup probe that exceeded 30 seconds remains preserved. Application CSS discovery is now explicitly scoped to `src`, and ignored local audit/copy/evidence files cannot supply CSS classes; [Tailwind's source-base guidance](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files) documents the syntax. No Webpack fallback was used in these runs.
+
+Future GitHub CI logs, coverage and browser evidence use revision/run/attempt artifact names, file hash indexes and explicit 90-day retention, including failed runs. The browser workflow uses one worker and zero retries and runs production checks even if development checks fail, once its production build succeeds. [GitHub's retention policy](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/configuring-the-retention-period-for-github-actions-artifacts-and-logs-in-your-organization) caps public-repository artifact retention at 90 days. Selected candidate results and failed traces will also be preserved in a separate draft verification archive in the existing repository, with upload/retrieval hashes; it stores evidence rather than approving an application release. Index generation is tested locally; candidate CI upload, archive upload, retrieval and digest verification are pending at this source checkpoint. Historical tracked evidence has not been removed.
+
+The existing base-revision remote CI failed documentation at the six ignored-file links, leaving browser and Lighthouse jobs skipped. That failed remote run is preserved independently of local repair checks. Candidate remote CI and the new TestSprite layout run remain pending here; the original blocked/inconclusive TestSprite artwork run is unchanged.
+
+## Evidence and remaining release limits
+
+Raw logs, structured results, frozen manifests and retained native failure bundles are under local-only `artifacts/l09-repeatability-2026-10-09/`. Failed runs are separate from successful reruns. The [local verification receipt](evidence/2026-10-09-validation-repeatability/verification.json) records 38 evidence hashes and the exact local scope without embedding signed recording links or credentials. Remote CI, external and archive-custody receipts are subsequent evidence, not implied by this local checkpoint. The final documentation-only check first failed on a sandbox temporary-cache rename restriction; its native workspace-cache retry is recorded separately.
+
+Physical pen/touch devices, manual screen-reader observations, low-memory/long-session and real two-machine/network modes, actual production-host update/rollback and final release approval remain separate. Automated browser/Axe/keyboard checks qualify their executed states and retain the documented compact color-dock target-size tradeoff. No physical-device or WCAG-conformance result is inferred from them.

+# S1 resource-cache recovery and L09 replay — 10 October 2026
+
+Application repair: `8e43eb7469beb22b92d59ff8a954f573ddece9d3`. Validation-only byte-comparison repair: `bd4a352090836792a647bfd3ad5025f77b2c183b`. The latter changes no application source. Work started on 9 October and continued after midnight in Europe/Istanbul. Evidence paths retain their initial session date.
+
+Latest validation-only follow-up: `2591829e403d543a15efe169aba4127edd137385`. It observes native activation before reopening a window and uses full Chromium headless mode for development. Application source is unchanged from the resource-recovery repair. Both previous failed runs and new verdicts retain their own revisions.
+
+## Recovery behavior
+
+The service worker captures its original cache handle at event arrival. Optional opening, reads and writes settle after rejection, synchronous exception or a 250 ms deadline. Static resources start their healthy network fetch immediately; default resources keep cache-first behavior and try the network after unavailable storage. Default opening and reading have separate deadlines and can together take up to 500 ms. Deadlines settle responses/event lifetimes; they do not abort native storage operations. A cache response arriving after its deadline is unavailable to that fallback; physical-device cache latency remains unqualified.
+
+Readable cached resources remain usable offline. A failed HTTP refresh also prefers a readable cached response. Unavailable cache plus failed network returns an explicit resource error, never substituted HTML. Worker bootstrap fragments retain the existing synthetic-response handling. Mandatory installation still requires a complete offline shell; activation and waiting-update ownership contracts remain intact. Warming uses the originally captured handle and does not reopen a retired bucket.
+
+## Retained failures and repairs
+
+- Before repair, emitted-worker probes: 15 failures /3 passes across 18 cases. The first harness attempt also recorded unhandled rejection noise; the corrected baseline retains the same 15 failures without that harness noise.
+- Before repair, native Chromium `open-reject`: Studio HTML loaded but active restoration did not finish after reload. Its trace and screenshot remain retained.
+- A preliminary candidate passed its full gate, but an additional HTTP-503 refresh check exposed a new race: the failed network response beat a readable cached 200. That failing check is retained. The repaired policy now prefers the readable cache; 54 focused checks across four files pass.
+- Final emitted-worker resource suite: 26 cases cover rejected/stalled opening, reads and writes; synchronous storage errors; exact cached bytes; failed refresh; bounded event lifetimes; unavailable offline resources and warming.
+- Prior documentation-only CI replay [37986316428](https://github.com/lxcario/PixiBun/actions/runs/37986316428), `5cdf03d`: 2,199 passes /one failure. Nearest-neighbor identity correctness exceeded its 5,000 ms runner timeout, reporting 6,288 ms. Performance/build/browser jobs did not complete. This does not rewrite the earlier `94bd345` passing run.
+- Byte comparison now uses native buffer equality for every byte of both the transformed output and unchanged input at all four original resolutions. Test count, default timeout, coverage policy and separate warmed performance limits are unchanged.
+- First scoped native candidate run: 29 passes /one failure, no retries. All 12 new fault cases pass across Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, restoring exact saved artwork and resource hashes. The existing Firefox drawing case completed all final application assertions, then failed `Browser.removeBrowserContext` with `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` during context teardown. Trace assessment is retained; the cause is not established, and this run remains failed.
+
+## Executed candidate checks
+
+The fresh six-stage local gate passes 2,226 tests /203 suites, documentation, strict types, lint, coverage, separate performance limits and production build. Coverage is 69.17% statements, 62.39% branches, 61.49% functions, 70.46% lines. RotSprite p90 of warmed batch means is 5.801 ms against the unchanged 10 ms limit. A preceding final-app gate measured 3.093 ms and also passed. These desktop batch measurements do not qualify individual-call latency or physical-device frame rates.
+
+Qualified local build: `IHzbF9f6G4oaf-1wpkS95`, 259 compiled files. Selected source/validation inputs: 706, aggregate `424774cc47769c984417021cb351a0d037abe31be57cfcb3046ca5e6fadb5d12`. Build/source freeze receipts bind subsequent runs to this candidate. The normal five-stage pre-push gate independently passes all 2,226 tests and publishes the two repair commits to the existing draft review branch.
+
+CI run [37992174340](https://github.com/lxcario/PixiBun/actions/runs/37992174340) passes its six-stage gate on Node 22.14.0, all 2,226 tests /203 suites and the unchanged performance limits. RotSprite warmed batch p90 is 2.253 ms. Its merge `cb00150c07fc58e2eb01bb09d21949ddc79dd162` and local candidate have the same Git tree, `9622eb475ec1d020cc06b717800204e32a5c1b54`. Automatic CI retrieval compares all 379 indexed files and original index bytes. The independently retrieved ZIP also matches its API digest; all embedded indexed files and the file set match locally.
+
+Fresh two-build replay: five passes /one measured Windows WebKit legacy-Blob fixture refusal, one worker and zero retries. All 259 previous compiled files match before and after. Native attachment records identify the actual buckets as `pixibun-v1.14.1-ad957550f6656b82f5f35162c8eabc19a45a1473` and `pixibun-v1.14.1-bd4a352090836792a647bfd3ad5025f77b2c183b` and preserve the artwork and optional metadata through update and rollback. This local proxy transition does not qualify production-host deployment or actual Safari legacy rollback.
+
+Fresh raw CI Lighthouse reports: Home accessibility 1.00, no small-target findings; Studio 0.96, seven small-target findings in each of three reports. All six have zero label/name mismatches. The API-verified reports are retained before their seven-day artifact expiry. Passing configured score thresholds does not close the remaining target/manual findings.
+
+Read-only [public-host baseline](https://pixibun.vercel.app/): Studio, worker, manifest and one observed JavaScript chunk return 200. The worker declares the older `ad95755` cache tag, not this candidate. Headers/digests are recorded sep
